hypotheses.claim: Annual MRCP-based surveillance in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is associated with improved detection and outcomes for CCA compared with non-surveillance, supporting risk-stratified imaging surveillance as an early-detection strategy in this high-risk population.
hypotheses.reasoning: A retrospective cohort directly compared MRCP surveillance vs non-surveillance in PSC and reported outcome differences, and PSC is a well-established premalignant condition. However, a reported case of intrahepatic CCA arising in small-duct PSC (a phenotype traditionally considered lower risk) with normal large-duct MRCP appearance shows that standard surveillance protocols may miss malignancy in subgroups, complicating universal application.

hypotheses.claim: Serum beta-hCG, reflecting tumor LHCGR upregulation, combined with conventional tumor markers (e.g., CA19-9/CEA) improves detection sensitivity and prognostic stratification for cholangiocarcinoma relative to conventional markers alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: A multi-omics discovery study identified LHCGR/beta-hCG as differentially expressed and correlated with stage, validated by IHC and serum measurement combined with routine markers. This is a single-population (Northeast Thailand, fluke-endemic) discovery study; broader reviews note that conventional serologic diagnostics generally remain insufficiently sensitive/specific for early-stage disease, so independent validation in non-endemic cohorts is needed.

hypotheses.claim: Plasma ctDNA detection of IDH1/2 mutations enables non-invasive identification of minimal residual disease and earlier recurrence detection in IDH-mutant cholangiocarcinoma, ahead of radiographic progression.
hypotheses.reasoning: Strong concordance between tissue and plasma IDH1/2 mutations and their established clinical actionability (ivosidenib) support ctDNA as a molecular residual disease marker. However, reviews of ctDNA in pancreatobiliary cancers emphasize that sensitivity for true early/localized disease (as opposed to postoperative MRD in a molecularly pre-selected subgroup) remains a barrier, limiting generalization to de novo early detection/screening.

hypotheses.claim: Low-pass whole-genome sequencing-based cfDNA fragmentomics (copy number, fragment size, other genome-wide features) can noninvasively detect biliary tract cancer and stratify postoperative risk, offering a scalable liquid-biopsy screening approach.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated model-development/validation study built and tested a cfDNA fragmentomics framework specifically for BTC detection and risk assessment. Broader liquid-biopsy literature cautions that sensitivity for stage I disease remains limited due to low tumor-derived analyte fraction, a general limitation likely also affecting fragmentomic approaches in early BTC.

hypotheses.claim: Targeted next-generation sequencing performed on cholangioscopy-guided brushings/biopsies improves diagnostic sensitivity for cholangiocarcinoma in extrahepatic biliary strictures compared with cytohistology and FISH alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: A prospective study of 104 patients with optimized single-operator cholangioscopy sampling showed NGS outperforming cytohistology/FISH. However, a separate prospective study found FISH has substantial false-negative rates (40-50%) driven by procedural/sampling factors, suggesting that molecular assay performance is highly dependent on sampling technique and may not generalize across all endoscopy settings.

hypotheses.claim: Massive parallel sequencing (e.g., Oncomine Comprehensive/Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assays) applied to ERCP-obtained bile fluid and brush cytology improves discrimination of malignant from benign biliary strictures beyond standard pathology.
hypotheses.reasoning: A prospective evaluation demonstrated added diagnostic value of MPS assays on biliary brushings/bile fluid. A comprehensive review of benign biliary strictures highlights how overlapping inflammatory/fibrotic features with malignancy make any single modality (including molecular assays validated in small prospective cohorts) insufficient alone, requiring integration with imaging and multidisciplinary review.

hypotheses.claim: Chronic Clonorchis sinensis/Opisthorchis viverrini infection induces measurable epigenetic, miRNA, and metabolite changes in blood/bile that could serve as early biomarkers of precancerous biliary lesions in endemic populations.
hypotheses.reasoning: Reviews synthesize mechanistic links between fluke-induced chronic inflammation and epigenetic/molecular alterations proposed as biomarkers. The same source explicitly notes that current evidence is largely preclinical/small-cohort without multi-center prospective validation, limiting confidence in near-term clinical utility.

hypotheses.claim: Multi-omic profiling of bile (16S microbiome, metabolomics, bile acid quantification) obtained during ERCP can distinguish PSC and benign biliary disease from cholangiocarcinoma, offering a route to earlier diagnosis in high-risk patients undergoing endoscopic evaluation.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated bile multi-omics biomarker discovery study directly compared PSC, CCA, and benign biliary disease bile samples. A related review on the bile acid-microbiome axis in biliary tract cancers highlights the complexity and bidirectionality of these interactions, which could introduce confounding and reduce biomarker specificity across different patient populations and disease stages.

hypotheses.claim: Patients with congenital choledochal cysts require lifelong biliary surveillance after cyst resection because malignant transformation risk persists for decades, and current follow-up intervals may be insufficiently long to capture late-onset cholangiocarcinoma.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple independent case reports document cholangiocarcinoma or other pancreatobiliary malignancy arising many years (up to nearly four decades) after choledochal cyst resection/diversion surgery, indicating that surveillance windows commonly used in practice may end prematurely. Evidence is case-report level, limiting generalizability, but the consistency across independently reported cases strengthens the hypothesis that extended surveillance intervals warrant systematic study.

hypotheses.claim: Diabetes mellitus and hepatitis B virus infection are independent and potentially synergistic risk factors for both intrahepatic and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, suggesting that patients with these comorbidities could be prioritized for risk-based early-detection strategies.
hypotheses.reasoning: A case-control study using conditional logistic regression and synergism indices found DM and HBV associated with CCA risk. However, epidemiologic transition data from an endemic Korean cohort suggest that metabolic risk factor contributions are evolving over time and vary regionally, meaning risk models built on one population's risk factor profile (e.g., DM/HBV) may require regional recalibration.

hypotheses.claim: Persistently elevated serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) over time, even without overt symptoms, is an accessible real-world signal associated with increased risk of downstream hepatobiliary and pancreatic malignancy, including cholangiocarcinoma, and could be incorporated into risk-stratified surveillance triggers.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large propensity-matched real-world cohort study found associations between persistently elevated GGT and hepatobiliary malignancy outcomes. The same study acknowledges GGT's inherent nonspecificity as a marker of alcohol use, metabolic dysfunction, and general hepatobiliary injury, which limits its standalone predictive value for cholangiocarcinoma specifically and necessitates combination with more specific markers.

hypotheses.claim: The epidemiologic profile of biliary tract cancers is shifting toward metabolic risk factors (obesity, MASLD, hypertension) alongside traditional inflammation-related causes, implying that metabolic risk indices should be integrated into future CCA early-detection risk models, particularly outside classically fluke-endemic regions.
hypotheses.reasoning: A 13-year regional cohort study documented increasing metabolic comorbidity burden among BTC patients in a historically inflammation-driven endemic area. A separate systematic review/meta-analysis on MASLD and GI tumors explicitly describes the MASLD-GI cancer relationship as 'controversial,' indicating that causal attribution and effect size for CCA specifically remain unsettled.

hypotheses.claim: Metformin use in diabetic patients is associated with reduced risk of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, suggesting metabolic modulation could be explored both as a chemopreventive strategy and as a factor to adjust for in risk-stratified surveillance models.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large Swedish nationwide cohort study examined metformin use and liver cancer subtype risk, including intrahepatic CCA. The study itself frames its central question as uncertain ('It is uncertain whether...'), reflecting that causality versus confounding-by-indication (e.g., healthier diabetic phenotype) has not been established, so this remains a preliminary, hypothesis-generating association.

hypotheses.claim: A combined biliary and serum CEA/CA19-9 multimarker model, validated across training and independent cohorts, improves diagnostic accuracy for distinguishing malignant from benign biliary strictures compared with either single marker or single fluid compartment (bile vs serum) alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: A retrospective cohort study with training/validation split plus a meta-analysis of 7 pooled studies supports improved ROC performance for a combined bile+serum marker model. The same source's meta-analysis reports heterogeneity across pooled studies, indicating variable marker cutoffs/assay platforms across centers that could limit reproducibility of the combined model in new settings.

hypotheses.claim: A dedicated blood-based cell-free DNA methylation test currently in prospective trial development can detect biliary tract cancers (including CCA) at earlier, potentially asymptomatic stages, offering a scalable non-invasive screening tool for high-risk populations.
hypotheses.reasoning: An actively registered clinical trial is specifically designed to evaluate a cfDNA methylation blood test for BTC screening, reflecting translational momentum toward this approach. As with other liquid biopsy modalities, published literature on GI cancers generally documents persistently limited sensitivity for stage I disease, so the trial's success is not yet established and the approach remains unproven pending results.

hypotheses.claim: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis is frequently misdiagnosed as cholangiocarcinoma on imaging and initial labs, indicating that improved multimodal diagnostic criteria (serum IgG4, histology, response to steroids) are needed to reduce false-positive 'cancer' calls and refine the true specificity of any early-detection pathway for CCA.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple independent case reports and a mini-review document IgG4-SC mimicking perihilar/distal CCA leading to unnecessary radical surgery. One report specifically documents initially normal preoperative serum IgG4 with only delayed postoperative elevation, showing that even the primary diagnostic biomarker for this mimicker can be falsely reassuring, complicating differential diagnosis algorithms.

hypotheses.claim: Rare benign biliary mimickers such as eosinophilic cholangitis can closely simulate cholangiocarcinoma on imaging and tumor markers, underscoring the need for tissue-based or eosinophil-count-based discriminators before committing patients to major hepatobiliary resection in ambiguous 'early-detected' lesions.
hypotheses.reasoning: A case report demonstrates radical pancreaticoduodenectomy planned for suspected CCA based on imaging/labs, later found to be eosinophilic cholangitis intraoperatively. This is a single case, so while illustrative of a real diagnostic pitfall relevant to any early-detection pathway, it provides limited generalizable epidemiological weight.

hypotheses.claim: Combining advanced peroral cholangioscopy with confocal laser endomicroscopy improves early detection of extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, particularly tumors with periductal infiltrative growth that evade conventional luminal-surface sampling techniques.
hypotheses.reasoning: A histomorphology-oriented review specifically frames cholangioscopy plus optical diagnostic technologies as addressing the sampling limitations of periductal infiltrative eCCA. The same review acknowledges that conventional endoscopic sampling techniques fundamentally assess only the luminal mucosal surface, meaning even advanced optical add-ons may still under-sample submucosal/periductal tumor extension without further technical refinement.

hypotheses.claim: Newer single-use peroral cholangiopancreatoscopes increase diagnostic yield for tumor detection in indeterminate biliary strictures compared with older reusable systems, potentially enabling earlier tissue-confirmed diagnosis.
hypotheses.reasoning: A case series reported 100% adequate tissue yield with a novel single-use cholangiopancreatoscope system for indeterminate strictures. However, the series comprised only 12 patients, which is insufficient to establish generalizable diagnostic yield improvements over existing systems.

hypotheses.claim: Systematic recognition and molecular characterization of biliary intraepithelial neoplasia (BilIN) and intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct (IPNB) as histologic precursor lesions could enable a pre-invasive detection and surveillance paradigm for cholangiocarcinoma analogous to pancreatic IPMN management.
hypotheses.reasoning: Pathology reviews and case reports establish BilIN/IPNB as recognized precursor lesions with distinct molecular/morphologic features, paralleling pancreatic precursor lesion paradigms. The same review notes that accurate diagnosis of these precursor lesions is complicated by overlapping histologic features, fragmented sampling, and under-recognition, which currently limits their practical use as a reliable early-detection trigger.

hypotheses.claim: Germline genetic testing for hereditary predisposition genes (e.g., BAP1, homologous recombination pathway genes) in biliary tract cancer patients identifies a clinically meaningful subset with hereditary cancer syndromes, supporting cascade testing and enhanced surveillance in relatives as an early-detection strategy.
hypotheses.reasoning: A prospective single-center study found pathogenic germline variants in a meaningful proportion of BTC patients meeting testing criteria, supporting genetic counseling referral pathways. However, a patient-outcome survey of BAP1-TPDS carriers found substantial gaps in patient knowledge and compliance with surveillance recommendations, indicating that genetic identification alone does not guarantee effective downstream early-detection behavior.

hypotheses.claim: Specific ultrasound morphological features of gallbladder polyps (beyond simple size thresholds) can better discriminate neoplastic from non-neoplastic polyps, potentially refining current size-based surveillance/cholecystectomy guidelines and enabling earlier identification of premalignant lesions.
hypotheses.reasoning: A systematic review/meta-analysis identified specific US features with significant diagnostic odds ratios for neoplastic polyps, and a UK cost-effectiveness analysis models ultrasound surveillance strategies for sub-10mm polyps. A separate review on asymptomatic gallstone/polyp management notes ongoing debate about surgical thresholds and calls for precision-medicine integration, indicating current size-based guidelines are still contested and morphology-based refinements are not yet standardized.

hypotheses.claim: AI/large language model-assisted interpretation of gallbladder polyp ultrasound reports could help standardize risk stratification and reduce unnecessary cholecystectomies while flagging higher-risk polyps for closer follow-up, indirectly supporting earlier detection of malignant transformation.
hypotheses.reasoning: A comparative study evaluated multiple LLM input strategies for gallbladder polyp ultrasound interpretation, showing feasibility. This is an early feasibility/comparative study without prospective clinical validation against outcomes, so its real-world impact on early cancer detection remains speculative.

hypotheses.claim: Aberrant protein glycosylation patterns (e.g., fucosylation, glycoprotein alterations) identified in cholangiocarcinoma tumor microenvironments represent candidate circulating biomarkers for earlier, more specific detection than CA19-9 alone, drawing on analogous glycoproteomic progress in pancreatic cancer.
hypotheses.reasoning: Glycosylation-related prognostic gene signatures have been described in CCA tumor tissue, and fucosylation is mechanistically linked to digestive cancer pathogenesis, with glycoproteomic biomarker panels already showing promise in the closely related pancreatic cancer field. However, the pancreatic cancer glycoproteomic evidence is disease-specific, and direct translation and validation of analogous circulating glycan biomarkers specifically for early-stage CCA detection has not yet been demonstrated in the retrieved CCA-specific study, which focused on prognosis/immunotherapy rather than early detection.

hypotheses.claim: Higher consumption of sugar-sweetened (and possibly artificially sweetened) beverages is associated with increased risk of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, identifying a modifiable dietary exposure that could inform population-level risk stratification for early-detection or prevention programs.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large pooled analysis of prospective cohorts specifically examined beverage intake and liver cancer subtypes, including intrahepatic CCA, finding associations. As an observational pooled-cohort design, residual confounding by obesity, diabetes, and overall dietary pattern (all independently linked to biliary tract cancer risk in other retrieved evidence) cannot be fully excluded, so causal contribution of beverage intake per se to CCA risk remains uncertain.

hypotheses.claim: Plasma ctDNA sequencing panels detecting IDH1 R132 hotspot mutations can serve as an early, non-invasive marker for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, given documented high concordance between tumor tissue and plasma IDH1/2 mutation status.
hypotheses.reasoning: IDH1-mutant CCA is a molecularly defined subtype with strong tissue-plasma concordance reported for MRD monitoring; the same mutation specificity could in principle be leveraged for screening in at-risk populations, though current evidence is mainly for MRD/recurrence, not de novo screening, and IDH1 mutations are absent in most CCA (only a subset), limiting panel sensitivity as a stand-alone test.

hypotheses.claim: FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement detection via targeted DNA or RNA-based liquid biopsy assays could enable earlier molecular subtyping and detection of a clinically distinct, indolent-appearing intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma subtype before overt radiologic progression.
hypotheses.reasoning: FGFR2 fusions are recurrent, clinically actionable, and well characterized in iCCA tissue genomics; however, fusion detection in cfDNA is technically harder than point mutations (breakpoint heterogeneity, low structural variant allele fraction), and current evidence focuses on treatment selection rather than validated early-detection performance.

hypotheses.claim: Cell-free DNA methylation signatures (genome-wide or targeted panels) in blood can distinguish early-stage biliary tract cancer from benign biliary disease, as being tested in dedicated screening assays.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated clinical trial is prospectively validating a cfDNA methylation blood test for BTC screening, and methylation-based liquid biopsy is a leading MCED modality; however, general GI liquid-biopsy reviews note sensitivity remains limited in stage I disease due to low tumor DNA shedding, a key caveat for very early detection.

hypotheses.claim: Bile-based cell-free DNA and ctDNA (obtained during ERCP) has higher tumor fraction than plasma and may improve sensitivity for early molecular detection of biliary strictures of uncertain etiology.
hypotheses.reasoning: Bile is proximal to the tumor and reviews highlight bile ctDNA/cfDNA as a promising analyte source distinct from and potentially more sensitive than blood; comparative sensitivity/specificity data across large cohorts is still limited.

hypotheses.claim: Global hypermethylation of N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-modified RNA in bile can distinguish pancreatobiliary malignancy (including biliary tract cancer) from benign biliary stone disease with high discriminative power.
hypotheses.reasoning: A proof-of-concept bile m6A ELISA study reported an AUC of 1.00 distinguishing pancreatic/biliary tract cancer from stones, but the cohort was very small (BTC n=35) and unreplicated, so this is an early exploratory finding requiring validation before it can be considered a reliable detection biomarker.

hypotheses.claim: Bile clusterin (CLU) protein, detectable via optic-fiber biosensor or ELISA during endoscopy, is a candidate biomarker for real-time, in vivo early diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma in patients with indeterminate biliary strictures.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple independent proteomic studies (>580 and >640 subject cohorts) identified and validated bile clusterin as elevated in CCA and built diagnostic/deep-learning models and a biosensor for real-time detection, providing a relatively mature evidence base for this candidate, though external validation across diverse populations and stages is still needed.

hypotheses.claim: Circulating microRNA panels (e.g., combinations of serum miRNAs altered downstream of p53 dysfunction) can improve non-invasive diagnostic sensitivity for cholangiocarcinoma beyond CA19-9 alone, particularly in liver-fluke-endemic populations.
hypotheses.reasoning: Several independent studies report circulating miRNA panels distinguishing CCA from controls with validation in serum cohorts, including in Opisthorchis viverrini/Clonorchis sinensis-endemic settings, but most cohorts are small, single-center, and miRNA studies to date emphasize prognosis/diagnosis in already-symptomatic patients rather than true pre-symptomatic screening.

hypotheses.claim: Hypermethylation of specific tumor-suppressor gene promoters (epigenetic field defect) in cholangiocyte DNA driven by chronic Opisthorchis viverrini infection may serve as an early risk-stratification biomarker preceding overt malignant transformation.
hypotheses.reasoning: Scoping review evidence supports a predominant hypermethylation phenotype in liver-fluke-associated CCA linked to Wnt/beta-catenin pathway dysregulation, suggesting methylation-based risk stratification is biologically plausible in endemic populations, but current literature remains mostly descriptive/mechanistic rather than validated as a prospective screening tool.

hypotheses.claim: Serial per-oral cholangioscopy-guided biopsy combined with molecular marker testing may not substantially outperform standard ERC/cytology for detecting incident CCA within 12 months in PSC patients, indicating a need for molecular (rather than purely visual) surveillance adjuncts.
hypotheses.reasoning: A prospective POCS follow-up study in PSC patients suggests visual/structural surveillance alone has limitations, supporting the rationale for molecular biomarker-based surveillance strategies as a complement, though this hypothesis is more about a gap that molecular markers could fill than direct molecular evidence.

hypotheses.claim: A prospective PSC biobank cohort (serum/plasma) enables discovery and validation of blood-based molecular biomarkers (genetic, epigenetic, or protein) for early cholangiocarcinoma detection in this high-risk surveillance population.
hypotheses.reasoning: An ongoing national Swedish PSC surveillance cohort with yearly imaging and biobanking is explicitly designed to enable biomarker discovery for early CCA detection in this defined high-risk group, providing a strong translational research infrastructure, though results validating specific biomarkers from this cohort are not yet available in the retrieved literature.

hypotheses.claim: ERBB2 (HER2) amplification detectable by ctDNA-based testing can identify a molecularly distinct CCA subgroup at diagnosis, offering an opportunity for earlier molecular subclassification alongside standard workup.
hypotheses.reasoning: A documented case shows ERBB2 amplification detected by ctDNA and confirmed in tissue, demonstrating feasibility of liquid-biopsy detection of copy-number alterations in CCA; however this evidence is primarily about treatment-matching in advanced disease, not early/asymptomatic detection, and copy-number calling from cfDNA has lower sensitivity than point-mutation detection at low tumor fractions.

hypotheses.claim: BRAF V600E mutation, though present in only a small subset of CCA, is detectable by tumor-informed ctDNA assays and could support earlier, non-invasive molecular confirmation of malignancy in indeterminate biliary lesions where tissue is scant.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple CIViC entries confirm BRAF V600E occurs in CCA and is druggable, supporting its detectability, but its low prevalence in CCA overall limits its value as a broad early-detection marker; it is more useful as an adjunct actionable finding once malignancy is otherwise suspected.

hypotheses.claim: Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) detecting polysomy/aneuploidy in biliary brush cytology specimens improves sensitivity for early detection of malignant biliary strictures compared with cytology alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: A systematic review/meta-analysis specifically evaluated FISH diagnostic performance for biliary strictures, and a separate study found SNP microarray (higher-resolution than FISH) improved sensitivity over cytology alone in biliary brushings, jointly supporting molecular cytogenetic adjuncts to cytology, though definitions of 'positive FISH' vary across studies affecting reported accuracy.

hypotheses.claim: Genome-wide copy-number profiling (e.g., SNP microarray/OncoScan) of pancreaticobiliary brushing specimens can detect chromosomal alterations missed by conventional cytology, enabling earlier and more sensitive diagnosis of malignant biliary strictures.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated study directly compared OncoScan microarray to cytology using biopsy as reference in 128 brushing specimens, demonstrating improved detection; this is a single-study result and needs multi-center replication before being considered established.

hypotheses.claim: PRKACA/PRKACB gene fusions are highly specific molecular markers for intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPN) of the bile duct/pancreatobiliary system and could be used to molecularly identify this precursor lesion before progression to invasive cholangiocarcinoma.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated study found PRKACA/PRKACB fusions across most IOPN cases with reasonable sensitivity/specificity, supporting use as a lesion-defining biomarker for a bile duct precursor neoplasm; however IOPN is a rare entity and fusion testing has not yet been validated in a prospective early-detection screening context.

hypotheses.claim: GNAS and KRAS mutation profiling of biliary lesions can help distinguish intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct (IPNB) precursor lesions from other biliary neoplasms, informing risk stratification for progression to invasive CCA.
hypotheses.reasoning: Pathology reviews describe distinct precursor lesion categories (BilIN, IPNB, IOPN) with different molecular/genetic profiles relevant to large-duct vs small-duct iCCA; while GNAS/KRAS involvement in IPNB is analogous to pancreatic IPMN biology, specific mutation-frequency data in bile duct IPNB was not directly retrieved, so confidence is moderate-low.

hypotheses.claim: KRAS and CREBBP co-mutation signatures may represent a population-specific (e.g., Thai, liver-fluke-associated) early molecular signature distinguishing Opisthorchis viverrini-associated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma from other etiologies, useful for risk-stratified screening in endemic regions.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated cohort study of 112 iCCA patients and OV-infected/healthy controls identified this signature, but the study itself states it is observational and demonstrates association rather than causation, and requires replication in independent cohorts before use as a detection tool.

hypotheses.claim: Loss of ARID1A (SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex) expression/mutation, detectable by IHC or targeted sequencing, marks a distinct molecular subclass of cholangiocarcinoma and could contribute to a multi-gene early molecular classification panel.
hypotheses.reasoning: ARID1A is a validated cancer-relevant target and reviews note tumor suppressor gene involvement in iCCA pathways, but specific quantitative data on ARID1A alteration frequency or its detection performance in liquid biopsy for CCA was not retrieved, so this remains a lower-confidence, mechanistically-plausible hypothesis.

hypotheses.claim: CDKN2A (p16) promoter hypermethylation or homozygous deletion, detectable in bile or brush cytology specimens, may serve as an early molecular marker of malignant transformation in biliary epithelium, analogous to its established role as an early epigenetic event in other GI cancers.
hypotheses.reasoning: CDKN2A is a well-established tumor suppressor frequently silenced by methylation across cancers, and hypermethylation phenotypes have been described in fluke-associated CCA; however, no CCA-specific bile/brush CDKN2A methylation validation study was directly retrieved, so this is an extrapolated hypothesis.

hypotheses.claim: SMAD4 loss-of-function alterations, reflecting TGF-beta pathway inactivation, could be incorporated into targeted mutation panels for cholangiocarcinoma molecular subtyping, similar to their established diagnostic role in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
hypotheses.reasoning: SMAD4 is a validated tumor-suppressor target with known TGF-beta pathway relevance in GI cancers and is cited among tumor suppressor genes in iCCA reviews, but direct evidence of its utility for CCA early detection (versus prognosis) was not specifically retrieved.

hypotheses.claim: MSI-high/mismatch repair-deficient status, while present in only a minority of CCA, can be detected via targeted NGS or IHC in biliary biopsy/cytology specimens and identifies a biologically and immunologically distinct subgroup relevant to early molecular triage.
hypotheses.reasoning: MSI-H/dMMR CCA is a recognized, clinically actionable molecular subtype confirmed by real-world studies, supporting its detectability by routine molecular testing; however, its low prevalence in CCA limits its standalone utility for population-level early detection versus subtype triage.

hypotheses.claim: Wnt/beta-catenin pathway epigenetic dysregulation (via hypermethylated pathway regulator genes) in Opisthorchis viverrini-associated cholangiocarcinoma represents a mechanistic basis for methylation-panel biomarkers that could be validated for pre-malignant risk detection in endemic populations.
hypotheses.reasoning: The scoping review directly links epigenetic biomarkers to Wnt/beta-catenin pathway dysregulation in fluke-associated CCA, providing mechanistic rationale, but notes this area is understudied/neglected with limited large-scale validation to date.

hypotheses.claim: Telomere length shortening and/or aberrant telomerase activity in cholangiocyte or peripheral blood DNA could serve as an adjunct biomarker for staging malignant risk/transformation, based on general principles of telomere biology in cancer detection.
hypotheses.reasoning: A broad review supports telomere length/telomerase activity as biomarkers distinguishing benign from malignant tissue across cancers generally, but no CCA-specific validation data were retrieved, making this a lower-confidence, extrapolated hypothesis pending disease-specific studies.

hypotheses.claim: Menin (MEN1 gene product) functional loss may play a tumor-suppressive role specific to cholangiocarcinoma, and its status could be explored as a novel molecular marker distinguishing CCA biology from other MEN1-associated neoplasms.
hypotheses.reasoning: A review specifically states menin suppresses cholangiocarcinoma (among other cancers), which is a novel and less-established finding relative to canonical CCA drivers like FGFR2/IDH1; further primary data would be needed to assess its detection utility, so confidence is modest.

hypotheses.claim: A multi-cancer early detection (MCED) blood test incorporating cfDNA methylation and fragmentomic features, validated across cancer types in large case-control cohorts, could be adapted/refined specifically to improve detection sensitivity for biliary tract cancers, which are typically underrepresented in current MCED panels.
hypotheses.reasoning: Large MCED trials and reviews support the general feasibility of cfDNA methylation-based pan-cancer detection, and a BTC-specific cfDNA methylation trial is underway, but MCED assays generally have lower sensitivity for rare, low-shedding cancers like CCA, especially at early stage, as noted in liquid biopsy reviews.

PMID:42196390.snippet: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and biliary tract cancers (BTCs) remain highly lethal gastrointestinal malignancies because of late presentation, marked molecular heterogeneity, and limited durable benefit from conventional systemic therapy. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in both diseases, focusing on practice-informing clinical trials, biomarker-driven treatment strategies, and translational insights into tumor biology and resistance. In PDAC, progress includes refinement of perioperative management, broader germline and somatic testing, recognition of DNA damage repair-deficient subsets, and development of KRAS-directed therapies and rational combination strategies. PMID:42123365.title: Advances in In Vitro Diagnostics for Cholangiocarcinoma: From Biomarker Discovery to Artificial Intelligence.
PMID:42123365.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly aggressive malignancy that is difficult to diagnose early and carries a poor prognosis. Conventional serological diagnostics are limited by inadequate sensitivity and the risks of invasive procedures, resulting in most patients being diagnosed at an advanced stage. In recent years, liquid biopsy has emerged as a novel approach for non-invasive and dynamic molecular tumor monitoring by detecting biomarkers such as circulating tumor cells (CTCs), extracellular vesicles (EVs), circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and clusterin (CLU). PMID:42353153.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) in Northeast Thailand is characterized by late diagnosis and poor prognosis, creating a critical need for effective early-detection biomarkers. This study utilized a multi-omics approach to identify novel diagnostic targets and improve CCA screening. Interaction network analysis subsequently identified its circulating ligand, beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), as a highly translatable clinical target. PMID:42136955.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma in Small-Duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis Associated With Crohn Disease: First Reported Case and Surveillance Implications.
PMID:42136955.snippet: Small-duct primary sclerosing cholangitis (sd-PSC) is traditionally regarded as a milder variant of PSC with a lower risk of hepatobiliary malignancy. Its association with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) remains unexplored. A 61-year-old woman with newly diagnosed Crohn disease presented with weight loss, anemia, and a liver mass initially suspected as hepatocellular carcinoma; biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated iCCA (CK7+/CK19+/Arginase-). MRCP showed normal large ducts with focal intrahepatic dilatation; liver biopsy demonstrated periductal onion-skin fibrosis diagnostic of sd-PSC. This report documents the first instance of metastatic iCCA in sd-PSC-CD, challenging current hepato-biliary malignancy surveillance paradigms in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.

PMID:42435161.title: Epidemiology of primary sclerosing cholangitis in general and IBD populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
PMID:42435161.snippet:
Background & aims

Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver condition that is closely associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). PSC is associated with substantial long-term hepatobiliary morbidity, including an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Reported prevalence and incidence estimates of PSC vary widely across different populations and study designs. This meta-analysis aims to provide an updated estimate of the prevalence of PSC in the general and IBD populations, and PSC incidence in the general population.

PMID:41964937.title: Annual magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography surveillance outcomes in individuals with primary sclerosing cholangitis.

Background

PMID:30422487.title: Clonorchiasis and Opisthorchiasis
PMID:30422487.snippet: Three trematodes belonging to the family Opithorchiidae cause human infections that primarily target the liver and biliary tract. They are Clonorchis sinensis, Opisthorchis viverrine, and Opisthorchis felineus. The 3 liver flukes differ slightly in size, ultrastructure, and epidemiology. They have similar complex life cycles, modes of transmission, and clinical implications. Thus, common features of infection caused by these parasites will be the focus of this activity, and where applicable, important differences will be discussed. The World Health Organization (WHO) classifies these parasites as significant neglected tropical diseases, and an estimated 27 million people are infected.[WHO. PMID:42221312.title: The role of liver fluke invasion in the pathogenesis of cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:42221312.snippet: Infections with the liver flukes Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini are currently endemic in Southeast and East Asia. Their limited ecological and geographical distribution is caused by environmental factors and culinary habits of the human population. Climate change, globalization, increasing human mobility, and environmental changes affecting the reservoir of zoonotic infections may change the epidemiology of trematodes. The species C. sinensis and O. viverrini have been recognized as biological carcinogens leading to the development of biliary tract cancer. This paper presents the epidemiology of infections with the above species, and summarizes the known mechanisms of cholangiocarcinogenesis induced by parasitic invasion.

Infections with liver flukes (Clonorchis sinensis, Opisthorchis viverrini, and O. felineus) cause high burden. However, no comprehensive review of these mechanistic models has yet been undertaken.

Methods

In this systematic review, we searched six major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Korea Med, Cochrane, China National Knowledge Infrastructure [CNKI], and Wanfang Data) for studies published up to 14 May 2025, to identify and evaluate mechanistic models of liver fluke infections. PMID:41919759.title: Clonorchis sinensis and cholangiocarcinoma: molecular mechanisms and biomarker advances.
PMID:41919759.snippet: Clonorchis sinensis, a common food-borne liver fluke in East Asia, is a Group 1 carcinogen strongly linked to cholangiocarcinoma. In recent years, molecular biology and multi-omics studies have revealed that this parasite drives chronic inflammation of the bile duct epithelium, epigenetic abnormalities, and the formation of precancerous lesions. Concurrently, circulating miRNAs, DNA methylation patterns, differential protein expression, metabolite profiles, and parasite-specific antigens have been proposed as potential early molecular biomarkers, which offers new avenues for the non-invasive detection of precancerous conditions. PMID:41138780.title: Can flukes cause cancer? Insight into molecular links between parasites and carcinogenesis.
PMID:41138780.snippet: Cancer deaths are increasing year by year worldwide. Many factors contribute to the development of cancer, including genetic and epigenetic factors, as well as environmental factors such as diet, physical activity, stimulants (tobacco, alcohol), exposure to excessive UV radiation, stress, and infections. In recent years, many studies have shown a strong correlation between parasitic infections and the oncogenic process leading to the development of human cancers. Studies indicate an association between progressive inflammation, risk of infection, or bacterial/viral co-infection during parasitosis and oncogenesis. PMID:41904891.title: Molecular endoscopy with next-generation sequencing improves diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma in patients with extrahepatic biliary strictures.
PMID:41904891.snippet:
Background & aims

Differentiating benign from malignant extrahepatic biliary strictures remains a diagnostic challenge, despite advances in sampling techniques and ancillary tests. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) may improve diagnostic performance and enable essential molecular profiling for malignancies. We aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of targeted NGS compared to cytohistology and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), using samples exclusively collected via optimized single-operator cholangioscopy.

Methods

PMID:40689505.title: The incidence and predictors of false-negative pancreatobiliary fluorescence in situ hybridization (PB-FISH) in biliary strictures: A prospective study.
PMID:40689505.snippet:
Background

Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is recommended as part of multimodality sampling in the evaluation of biliary strictures, but can be false negative in 40%-50% cases. The aim of this study was to comprehensively assess predictors of false-negative FISH in patients with biliary strictures.

Methods

Patients undergoing tissue sampling for biliary strictures from October 20 to February 22 were prospectively enrolled (NCT04572711). Procedural factors such as sampling techniques, order, and utilization of combination sampling were recorded. Results of an optimized pancreatobiliary FISH panel with locus-specific probes for 1q21, 7p12, 8q24, and 9p21 were reported per guidelines. Statistical analyses were performed using BlueSky Statistics v.10.3.1, R package v8.

PMID:39941254.title: Diagnostic Approach to Biliary Strictures.
PMID:39941254.snippet: Biliary strictures represent a narrowing of the bile ducts, leading to obstruction that may result from benign or malignant etiologies. Accurate diagnosis is crucial but challenging due to overlapping features between benign and malignant strictures. This review presents a comprehensive diagnostic approach that integrates biochemical markers, imaging modalities, and advanced endoscopic techniques to distinguish between these causes. Imaging tools such as ultrasound, MRI/MRCP, and CECT are commonly used, each with distinct advantages and limitations. Furthermore, endoscopic procedures such as ERCP and EUS are key in tissue acquisition, enhancing diagnostic accuracy, especially for indeterminate or complex strictures. PMID:39273408.title: Implementing Massive Parallel Sequencing into Biliary Samples Obtained through Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography for Diagnosing Malignant Bile Duct Strictures.
PMID:39273408.snippet: Despite advancements in radiologic, laboratory, and pathological evaluations, differentiating between benign and malignant bile duct strictures remains a diagnostic challenge. Recent developments in massive parallel sequencing (MPS) have introduced new opportunities for early cancer detection and management, but these techniques have not yet been rigorously applied to biliary samples. We prospectively evaluated the Oncomine Comprehensive Assay (OCA) and the Oncomine Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assay (OPCCFA) using biliary brush cytology and bile fluid obtained via endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography from patients with bile duct strictures. The diagnostic performance of MPS testing was assessed and compared to the pathological findings of biliary brush cytology and primary tissue. Mutat

PMID:39128126.title: Benign Biliary Strictures: A Comprehensive Review.
PMID:39128126.snippet: Benign biliary strictures (BBS) ensue from inflammatory conditions (e.g., chronic pancreatitis) or post surgery (e.g., cholecystectomy and liver transplant). High-quality cross-sectional imaging studies such as computed tomography or magnetic resonance cholangiopancre atography are essential in the diagnosis and planning of therapeutic interventions and in ruling out malignancy. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with dilation and stenting is the mainstay treatment for BBS, while surgery is reserved for failed endoscopy or refractory cases.

PMID:41912863.title: Circulating tumor DNA-based detection of molecular residual disease in isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant cholangiocarcinoma for biomarker-guided therapy.
PMID:41912863.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), particularly the IDH-mutant subtype, presents major clinical challenges because it is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage and carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence. Detecting minimal residual disease (MRD) is crucial, as it enables early identification of patients at high risk of relapse, guiding personalized adjuvant therapy to prevent recurrence and improve survival. Standard imaging modalities are unable to reliably detect microscopic MRD. In contrast, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for MRD detection in IDH-mutant CCA, supported by the strong concordance between IDH1/2 mutations identified in tumor tissue and those found in plasma. PMID:42145022.title: Advances and applications of liquid biopsy approaches in hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) cancers: a literature review.
PMID:42145022.snippet:
Background and objective

Hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) cancers, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), are among the deadliest malignancies due to late-stage diagnosis and limited curative options. Conventional tissue biopsies are often invasive and insufficient for longitudinal monitoring. This review synthesizes the current available literature on liquid biopsy, a minimally invasive approach that uses analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in serum, plasma, or bile, to enable better early detection, surveillance, and treatment monitoring of HPB cancers.

A search of PubMed, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Scopus, and Google Scholar

PMID:41873318.title: Integrating Circulating Tumor DNA (ctDNA) Into Postoperative Surveillance After the Resection of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Proposed Hybrid Imaging-Molecular Framework.
PMID:41873318.snippet: Recurrence after curative-intent resection remains common in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) and continues to limit long-term survival. Although repeat liver resection may benefit carefully selected patients, this opportunity is often lost because recurrence is detected only after radiographic progression. Postoperative surveillance relies primarily on cross-sectional imaging, which performs well for macroscopic disease but lacks sensitivity for microscopic residual tumor. Consequently, relapse is frequently recognized only after structural visibility, when tumor biology may already be unfavorable. PMID:41883993.title: Circulating Tumor DNA in Cholangiocarcinoma: A Precision Oncology Roadmap.
PMID:41883993.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a rare but aggressive malignancy with a rising global incidence and few therapeutic options for advanced disease. In recent decades, precision oncology for CCA has advanced rapidly, particularly through the development of targeted therapies for patients with actionable genetic alterations. These therapies have markedly prolonged survival and improved other clinical outcomes among patients with unresectable, advanced CCA. The implementation of precision oncology largely depends on detecting genetic mutations to guide patient selection and treatment, using tumor tissue biopsies or liquid biopsies, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from blood or bile. As a minimally invasive biomarker, ctDNA shows great promise for transforming the clinical management of CCA.

PMID:41866828.title: Liquid biopsy biomarkers for early detection of gastrointestinal cancers: Current landscape and emerging technologies.
PMID:41866828.snippet: Early detection of gastrointestinal (GI) cancers remains a critical unmet clinical need, as most patients are diagnosed at advanced stages when prognosis is poor. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a transformative approach for minimally invasive cancer detection by analysing tumour-derived analytes in blood and other body fluids. Recent advances in circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) sequencing, cell-free DNA methylation profiling, fragmentomics, extracellular vesicle and exosome characterisation, circulating tumour cell isolation and tumour-educated platelets have markedly improved sensitivity and specificity for detecting incipient malignancies. PMID:41487574.title: Liquid biopsy in biliary tract cancers: early diagnosis, precision therapy, and prognostic evaluation.
PMID:41487574.snippet: Biliary tract cancers represent a heterogeneous group of malignancies, including gallbladder cancer, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, and distal cholangiocarcinoma. These cancers share several common characteristics, such as challenges in early diagnosis, aggressive biological behavior, limited treatment options, and a propensity for drug resistance, all of which contribute to a notably poor prognosis for patients. Therefore, discovering new tumor biomarkers is urgently needed for early diagnosis, personalized treatment, and the prediction and monitoring of treatment effectiveness. PMID:41094495.title: Exploring the role of miR-221/222 in gastrointestinal cancers: implications for innovative therapeutic strategies.
PMID:41094495.snippet: MicroRNAs, also known as miRNAs, have a substantial part in regulating different essential cellular functions through post-transcriptional mechanisms. The MiR-221/222 family of genes is commonly disrupted in various forms of gastrointestinal (GI) cancer. Gastrointestinal cancers are the most commonly occurring cancerous growths across the world, with a significant number of cases and fatalities. PMID:40647454.title: Advancing Cholangiocarcinoma Diagnosis: The Role of Liquid Biopsy and CRISPR/Cas Systems in Biomarker Detection.
PMID:40647454.snippet: Background/Objectives: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy of the biliary tract with limited diagnostic tools for early detection. Current serum markers, such as CA19-9, lack specificity and sensitivity, particularly in early-stage disease, which hinders the effectiveness of curative interventions. PMID:41781899.snippet:
Background

Biliary tract cancers (BTCs) in East Asia have traditionally been linked to inflammation-related etiologies. However, metabolic risk factors are increasingly contributing to BTC development. Temporal trends in BTC epidemiology remain underexplored in the Korean population. This study aimed to review 13-year trends in BTCs, focusing on metabolic and inflammatory comorbidities, in a southeastern Korean cancer center historically characterized by a high incidence of inflammation-related BTCs.

PMID:42184304.title: Metformin use and the risk of liver cancer in a Swedish population-based cohort study.
PMID:42184304.snippet:
Background

It is uncertain whether medication with metformin decreases the risk of liver cancer. This study aimed to test the hypotheses that use of metformin decreases the risk of developing both main subtypes of liver cancer, that is, hepatocellular carcinoma and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

Methods

This nationwide population-based cohort study included all individuals who had dispensed anti-diabetic medications between 2005 and 2018 in Sweden, except for those with a history of viral hepatitis. PMID:41992238.title: The evolving role of OMICS in gastrointestinal tumor biology and clinical practice.
PMID:41992238.snippet: Due to late diagnosis, high molecular diversity, and limited response to therapeutic intervention, gastrointestinal (GI) cancers result in a considerable number of cancer-related deaths. Classic clinicopathological classification and single omics analysis fail to adequately convey the extensive biological complexity related to progression of disease, developed therapy resistance and recurrence of the disease. As a result, the recent introduction of integrated multi-omics including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and spatial profiling as well as the emerging use of liquid biopsy is substantially reshaping our understanding of and clinical approach to GI cancers. PMID:42094822.title: Advances in cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers for the diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of leptomeningeal metastases (Review).
PMID:42094822.snippet: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is an aggressive complication characterized by the dissemination of malignant cells to the leptomeninges, typically resulting in rapid neurological deterioration and poor prognosis. Clinical diagnosis and management are impeded by non-specific symptoms and the limited sensitivity of conventional cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology. Consequently, CSF biomarkers have emerged as critical tools for diagnosis, treatment monitoring and prognostic evaluation. The present review summarizes recent advancements in CSF biomarkers, categorizing them into proteins, nucleic acids and metabolites. PMID:41296409.title: Advances in Multi-Omics Research on Biomarkers of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:41296409.snippet: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a rare yet aggressive malignancy characterized by late-stage diagnosis and poor prognosis. Recent advancements in multi-omics technologies have significantly enhanced the understanding of the molecular features and complex biological mechanisms of iCCA. These approaches have revealed disease molecular heterogeneity and identified biomarkers linked to disease progression, patient prognosis, and therapeutic outcomes. This review synthesizes findings from multi-omics studies, highlighting their clinical implications and advancing the application of precision oncology in iCCA management.

PMID:42165910.snippet: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage due to the lack of effective screening tools, resulting in limited therapeutic options and poor survival outcomes. PMID:41652428.title: Circulating tumor DNA-guided early detection and minimal residual disease monitoring in pancreatic and biliary cancers: evidence, barriers, and opportunities.
PMID:41652428.snippet: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and biliary tract cancers (BTCs) are characterized by dismal prognoses, largely because effective strategies for early detection are lacking and post-surgical relapse is common. Liquid biopsy—particularly circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis—offers a minimally invasive and highly specific approach to reshape the clinical management of these malignancies. PMID:42195126.title: The Papanicolaou Smear Reimagined: A Narrative Review of Cervicovaginal Cytology and Molecular Biospecimens for Ovarian Cancer Detection.
PMID:42195126.snippet: The Papanicolaou (Pap) smear, a cornerstone of cervical cancer prevention, has emerged as a compelling, though unconventional, biospecimen for the detection of ovarian cancer (OC). This structured narrative review synthesizes the evolving evidence on the utility of cervicovaginal cytology and molecular analysis of Pap test material for OC detection. PMID:41939239.snippet: Malignant transformation of choledochal cysts after internal drainage is a known risk, but presentation nearly four decades later is exceptional. We report a case of cholangiocarcinoma developing 38 years after cystoduodenostomy in a 39-year-old female. Diagnosis was confounded by a periampullary diverticulum, mimicking Lemmel's syndrome. Surgical resection is recommended to prevent complications, including malignant transformation. We report the case of a 68-year-old woman with a remote history of cholecystectomy who presented with acute pancreatitis. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography identified a CDC associated with dilatation of the common bile duct. Most patients eventually require liver transplantation or develop serious complications, the most severe being end-stage liver disease and cholangiocarcinoma. The global prevalence of PSC is rising and has been reported to reach up to 31.7 cases per 100,000 individuals, representing a significant challenge in both diagnosis and management. Background

Hepatic carcinosarcoma (HCS) is an extremely rare primary malignant liver tumor characterized by aggressive biological behavior, early invasion, and poor prognosis. Owing to its non-specific clinical manifestations and imaging features, preoperative diagnosis remains challenging.

PMID:42183187.title: Present and future of liver transplantation for cholangiocellular carcinoma: moving toward personalized multiparametric transplantability patterns.
PMID:42183187.snippet: Liver transplantation for cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) shifted from a contraindication to a promising therapeutic option for selected patients. Advances in neoadjuvant therapy and refined selection criteria resulted in long-term outcomes comparable to other accepted oncologic indications, particularly in perihilar CCA managed with standardized protocols and in intrahepatic CCA with favorable tumor biology. The future challenge is to develop a multiparametric biological selection, blending clinical, functional, histopathologic, molecular, and radiologic parameters to identify candidates with indolent disease behavior, thus maximizing oncologic benefit while ensuring appropriate use of limited graft resources.

PMID:42079574.snippet:

PMID:40368336.title: Glycoproteomics of Gastrointestinal Cancers and Its Use in Clinical Diagnostics.
PMID:40368336.snippet: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide, resulting in substantial economic costs. Because cancer is a complex, heterogeneous group of diseases affecting a variety of cells, its detection may sometimes be difficult. PMID:37770126.title: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for the diagnosis and management of cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:37770126.snippet: These guidelines for the diagnosis and management of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) were commissioned by the British Society of Gastroenterology liver section. PMID:41294651.snippet: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the deadliest malignancies due to late diagnosis and limited treatment options. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising, minimally invasive biomarker that could improve the clinical outcomes of patients with PDAC by enabling early disease detection, minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment, precise prognostication, and accurate treatment monitoring. PMID:42040584.title: Case Report: The complete radiological resolution of diffuse cholangitis in a HIV-positive patient with cryptosporidium infection after anti-retroviral therapy.
PMID:42040584.snippet: We present a case of an HIV-positive patient with AIDS cholangiopathy secondary to Cryptosporidium infection. Imaging examination showed intrahepatic and extrahepatic cholangitis without papillary stenosis and extrahepatic bile duct strictures, indicating mild bile duct disease. However, it failed to obtain positive results in fecal microscopy examinations. Alternatively, metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of a blood sample identified Cryptosporidium infection. The diagnostic power of mNGS is highly sensitive and can simultaneously identify various pathogens. To avoid irreversible damage to the biliary system, the rapid initiation of anti-HIV therapy restored the function of the immune system and led to the clinical resolution of cryptosporidiosis.

PMID:39941748.snippet: Pancreaticobiliary diseases can lead to significant morbidity and their diagnoses rely on imaging and endoscopy which are dependent on operator expertise. However, its use for pancreaticobiliary endoscopic modalities such as endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) and cholangioscopy remains scarce, with only few studies available. In this review, we delve into the current evidence, benefits, limitations, and future scope of AI technologies in pancreaticobiliary endoscopy.

PMID:37017301.title: FGFR2 testing in cholangiocarcinoma: translating molecular studies into clinical practice.
PMID:37017301.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a heterogeneous group of neoplasms burdened by a dismal prognosis. Several studies have investigated the genomic profile of CCA and identified numerous druggable genetic alterations, including FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements. PMID:42325301.title: Plant-based diet quality is associated with esophageal mucosa-associated microbiome profiles and disease severity in a high-risk Chinese population.
PMID:42325301.snippet:
Background

Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a major public health challenge in China. Diet is a modifiable risk factor, and the esophageal mucosa-associated microbiome may contribute to esophageal disease progression. However, population-based evidence integrating plant-based diet quality, esophageal microbiome profiles anddisease severity remains limited.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional study including 236 participants undergoing upper gastrointestinal screening in Linzhou, a high-risk region for ESCC. Dietary intake was assessed using a food frequency questionnaire, and plant-based diet indices, including the overall plant-based diet index (PDI), healthful plant-based diet index (hPDI) and unhealthful plant-based diet index (uPDI), were calculated.

PMID:42164524.title: The gut-liver/bile axis: Gut microbiota and bacterial extracellular vesicles remodeling hepatobiliary pathogenesis.
PMID:42164524.snippet: Global hepatobiliary disease burden is increasing, prompting gut-liver axis research. Gut microbiota-secreted bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) carry bioactive molecules affecting host immunity, inflammation, and metabolism. Whether BEVs actively or passively cause liver damage is unclear. This review suggests gut-derived BEVs trigger hepatic innate immunity and sterile inflammation. By combining current findings on how gut microbes, their BEVs, and hepatobiliary diseases interact, we improve the "gut-liver/bile axis" idea. Acknowledging BEVs' active part in disease offers new ways to use them as diagnostic markers and treatment targets, likely better managing hepatobiliary disorders.

Background

Case presentation

PMID:40434997.title: A recent update on the morphological classification of intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct: Correlation with postoperative prognosis and pathological features.
PMID:40434997.snippet:
Purpose

We proposed a novel morphological classification for intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct (IPNB) and evaluated its association with postoperative prognosis.

Methods

Forty-two IPNB patients who underwent surgical resection were classified morphologically into three types-branched (n = 10), main duct (n = 26), and mixed (n = 6)-based on preoperative imaging features indicating cystic and/or bile duct involvement. Among them, 32 patients with evaluable specimens were further categorized pathologically into Type 1 (n = 10) and Type 2 (n = 22). Patient characteristics and postoperative outcomes were analyzed.

Results

Intraepithelial neoplasia was more frequently observed in the branched type, whereas invasive carcinoma predominated in the main duct type.

PMID:38280751.title: Early Cancerous Lesions of the Pancreas and Ampulla: Current Concepts and Challenges.
PMID:38280751.snippet: Owing to the increased use of advanced imaging techniques, mass-forming (cystic/intraductal) preinvasive neoplasms are being detected much more frequently and they have rapidly become one of the main focuses of interests in medical field. These neoplasms have very distinctive clinical and radiographic findings, exhibit a spectrum of dysplastic transformation, from low-grade dysplasia to high-grade dysplasia, and may be associated with an invasive carcinoma. Accounting for about 5% to 10% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, they provide a curable target subset in an otherwise biologically dismal pancreas cancer category.

PMID:40361508.snippet: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a locally aggressive tumor associated with asbestos exposure. CIVIC:EID11508.title: IDH1 R132C OR IDH1 R132H OR IDH1 R132L OR IDH1 R132G OR IDH1 R132S — Low Grade Glioma (PREDICTIVE, level A, SUPPORTS SENSITIVITYRESPONSE)
CIVIC:EID11508.snippet: This phase 3 clinical trial was conducted to assess the progression free survival in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with Vorasidenib, an oral brain-penetrant inhibitor, which showed preliminary activity in mutant gliomas. The results showed significant improvement in progression-free survival for patients treated with vorasidenib compared to placebo (median progression-free survival, 27.7 months vs. 11.1 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.27 to 0.56; P<0.001). The hazard ratio for disease progression or death was 0.39 (95% CI, 0.27-0.56; p<0.001). Overall, vorasidenib significantly improved PFS and delayed the time to the next intervention in the treatment group, compared to the control group (placebo group).

PMID:42122162.title: Liquid Biopsy in Advanced Prostate Cancer.

PMID:41883972.title: Treatment of biliary tract cancer - essentials for clinical practice.
PMID:41883972.snippet: Biliary tract tumours represent a serious medical problem due to their high mortality rate. CIVIC:EID11249.snippet: In this phase III, randomized, open-label trial, 536 patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2 regimens, with at least one being for metastatic disease. The patients were randomized 1:1 to margetuximab 15 mg/kg or trastuzumab 6 mg/kg (loading dose of 8 mg/kg), each in 3-week cycles. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). The study found that margetuximab improved primary PFS over trastuzumab (HR, 0.76; 95% CI: 0.59 - 0.98; p = .03; median, 5.8 [95% CI: 5.5 - 7.0] months versus 4.9 [95% CI: 4.2 - 5.6] months). CIVIC:EID1113.snippet: In this two arm, Phase III study (NCT00878709) of the efficacy of a 12 month course of the TKI neratinib after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy of early stage HER2-positive breast cancer was assessed using invasive disease-free survival as primary endpoint. HER2 positivity was assessed via FISH. At 2 year follow-up, 70 vs. 109 disease-free survival events had occurred and disease-free survival rates were 93.9% vs. 91.6% (significant) in neratinib vs. placebo groups respectively. Distant disease-free survival and time to distant recurrence were similar in both groups. These results are an interesting contrast to results of long-term adjuvant therapy with trastuzumab (HERA) which did not show significant benefit.

Patients were HER2 positive with completely excised invasive BC, node positive or negative, and having undergone prior adjuvant or neo-adjuvant chemotherapy.  In the 3 arm study patients were given trastuzumab courses of 1 year, 2 years, or untreated. A significant difference in disease-free survival was seen with 220 DFS events out of 1693 in the observation arm versus 127 DFS events out of 1694 in the 1 year trastuzumab arm.  1 year adjuvant trastuzumab is currently the standard of care.

CIVIC:EID1499.snippet: ToGA, a Phase III study (NCT01041404) addressed use of trastuzumab in HER2 positive (overexpression or amplification) advanced gastric cancer, where chemotherapy using fluoropyrimidine-based and platinum-based combinations had been common practice.  Patients were given a chemotherapy regime containing capecitabine, flourouracil and cisplatin with (n=298) or without (n=296) trastuzumab, and had not been previously treated for metastatic cancer.  Study endpoint was overall survival, which was significantly different in the two populations (13.8 months with chemotherapy + trastuzumab and 11.1 months for chemotherapy alone).  The authors conclude that trastuzumab should be a standard option for HER2 positive advanced gastric cancer.

PMID:41109905.snippet:

CIVIC:EID1409.title: BRAF V600E — Skin Melanoma (PREDICTIVE, level A, SUPPORTS SENSITIVITYRESPONSE)
CIVIC:EID1409.snippet: Phase 3 randomized clinical trial comparing vemurafenib with dacarbazine in 675 patients with previously untreated, metastatic melanoma with the BRAF V600E mutation. CCA can be further classified into intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (pCCA), and distal cholangiocarcinoma (dCCA) depending on the anatomical location. Until recently, the treatment for advanced CCA has remained highly reliant on chemotherapy, with gemcitabine plus cisplatin used in first-line treatment. Recent developments have led to the addition of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) to the chemotherapy regimen, highlighting the promising potential of immunotherapies for CCA treatment. PMID:36248745.title: Comprehensive drug response profiling and pan-omic analysis identified therapeutic candidates and prognostic biomarkers for Asian cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:36248745.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is rare cancer with the highest incidence in Eastern and Southeast Asian countries. Advanced CCA patients rely on chemotherapeutic regimens that offer unsatisfied clinical outcomes. We developed a comprehensive drug response profiling to investigate potential new drugs using CCA cell lines from Thai and Japanese patients against 100 approved anti-cancer drugs. We identified two major CCA subgroups that displayed unique molecular pathways from our integrative pan-omic and ligand-induced pathway activation analyses. MEK and Src inhibitors specifically killed the CCA1 subgroup without causing cytotoxicity to the normal cholangiocyte. PMID:41969551.title: Emerging KRAS G12D inhibitor in the treatment of digestive system tumors: opportunities and challenges.
PMID:41969551.snippet: The KRAS G12D mutation, defined by substitution of glycine with aspartic acid at codon 12 within the GTP-binding region of the KRAS gene, occurs with particularly high prevalence in digestive system malignancies, especially pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and colorectal cancer (CRC). Oncogenic KRAS variants drive persistent activation of downstream signaling cascades, including the MAPK and PI3K pathways, thereby circumventing upstream regulation and fueling tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Because of its high intrinsic affinity for GTP/GDP and the lack of a readily accessible binding pocket, KRAS was long considered a difficult therapeutic target. CIVIC:EID12153.title: KAT6A::CREBBP Fusion — AML With KAT6A::CREBBP Fusion (DIAGNOSTIC, level B, SUPPORTS POSITIVE)
CIVIC:EID12153.snippet: This is an international retrospective study by International Berlin-Frankfurt-Munster (I-BFM) AML study group including 543 pediatric AML patients from 18 countries diagnosed between 1995-2005. The authors recorded 62 pediatric AML patients with t(8;16)(p11;p13) determined by karyotyping, FISH and/or RT-PCR. Complete karyotypes were available for 57/62 cases, of which 22 (38.6%) showed additional non-recurrent cytogenetic aberrations. The t(8;16)(p11;p13) results in a fusion of exons 15 or 16 of KAT6A (also known as MOZ or MYST3, located to chromosome 8p11) to exon 3-8 of CREBBP (located to chromosome 16p13). CIVIC:EID12154.snippet: This manuscript is the first report of a unique expression profile in pediatric AML with KAT6A::CREBBP gene fusion (known also as MOZ::CBP or MYST3::CREBBP). Genomic studies and gene expression profile analysis were performed for a de novo AML M5b diagnosed in a 10-year-old girl. Pathology evaluation showed 23% blast in peripheral blood and 80% blasts in bone marrow. Karyotype and FISH confirmed the t(8;16)(p11;p13), resulting in the KAT6A::CREBBP fusion, as the sole chromosome abnormality. Gene expression analysis results for this case were compared with five non-t(8;16) pediatric AML cases (two M1, one M4, two M5), and adult cases with t(8;16)(p11;p13). They found KAT6A::CREBBP fusion in 11.4% of nuclei by Interphase FISH. The authors combined chromosome, interphase, and metaphase FISH results. FISH analysis showed a cryptic, insertional translocation event resulting in a KAT6A::CREBBP fusion on an apparently normal 16p. The authors discuss that pediatric AML cases with KAT6A::CREBBP fusion over 1 month of age have similar clinical manifestations, but with poorer clinical outcomes compared with congenital cases. PMID:42279405.snippet: Background: Radiotherapy outcomes are determined by the balance between tumor control and normal tissue toxicity, both of which exhibit significant interpatient variability. PMID:42346643.title: Bridging Ancestry-Stratified Bias in Pharmacogenomics AI: Toward Metabolomics-Inclusive Multi-Omics Precision Medicine.
PMID:42346643.snippet: Pharmacogenomics AI offers significant potential for individualized drug therapy; however, its clinical benefits remain unevenly distributed. Models trained predominantly on European-ancestry data consistently underperform in non-European populations, with polygenic risk scores (PRS) showing an estimated 39-73% reduction in predictive accuracy in African-ancestry cohorts across complex traits. These disparities have driven increased interest in moving beyond single-layer genomic approaches. PMID:42183274.title: Multi-omics biomarkers for predicting resistance, hyperprogression, and immune-related toxicity during PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in lung cancer: a literature review.
PMID:42183274.snippet: Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and its ligand programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) have transformed the management of advanced lung cancer, yet most patients experience primary resistance, hyperprogressive disease (HPD), or clinically significant immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Multi-omics technologies now enable integrated interrogation of tumor, microenvironmental, host, and clinical determinants of these divergent outcomes. In this review, we first discuss the biological and clinical foundations of PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in non-small cell and small cell lung cancer, and summarize the spectrum of resistance, HPD, and irAEs observed in trials and real-world practice. PMID:42042050.title: Omics-Derived Prognostic Biomarkers in Tongue Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review with Risk-of-Bias Appraisal and Translational Prioritization.
PMID:42042050.snippet: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is clinically heterogeneous, and patients with a similar TNM stage can experience markedly different outcomes. We systematically reviewed omics-driven studies to identify prognostic TSCC biomarkers. Although fundamentally prognostic, we discussed their theoretical translational relevance regarding future clinical decisions-such as treatment stratification or surveillance intensity-while strictly framing them as preliminary, hypothesis-generating targets. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched for original human studies published between 2014 and 2024 using high-throughput genomic or transcriptomic profiling. PMID:39532242.title: Genetic, Epigenetic, and Microenvironmental Drivers of Cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:39532242.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive and heterogeneous malignancy of the biliary tree that carries a poor prognosis. Multiple features at the genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental levels have been identified to better characterize CCA carcinogenesis. Genetic alterations, such as mutations in IDH1/2, BAP1, ARID1A, and FGFR2, play significant roles in CCA pathogenesis, with variations across different subtypes, races/ethnicities, and causes. Epigenetic dysregulation, characterized by DNA methylation and histone modifications, further contributes to the complexity of CCA, influencing gene expression and tumor behavior. PMID:37174616.title: Mutational Landscape of Cholangiocarcinoma According to Different Etiologies: A Review.
PMID:37174616.snippet: Recent next-generation sequencing (NGS) studies on large cohorts of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) patients have clearly revealed the extreme intra- and inter-tumoral molecular heterogeneity that characterizes this malignancy. The lack of a stereotyped molecular signature in CCA makes the identification of actionable therapeutic targets challenging, making it mandatory to have a better understanding of the origin of such heterogeneity in order to improve the clinical outcome of these patients. Compelling evidence has shown that the CCA genomic landscape significantly differs according to anatomical subtypes and the underlying etiology, highlighting the importance of conducting molecular studies in different populations of CCA patients. PMID:41891942.title: ATM immunohistochemistry as an effective screening method for POLE variants among endometrial carcinomas lacking mismatch repair deficiency and p53 abnormalities.
PMID:41891942.snippet: The molecular classification of endometrial carcinomas (ECs) is now integrated into clinical practice. However, identification of polymerase-ε (POLE) variants remains reliant on DNA sequencing, which limits broader implementation. PMID:41644842.title: Analysis of DNA mismatch repair and microsatellite instability in molecular typing of endometrial carcinoma.
PMID:41644842.snippet: DNA mismatch repair (MMR)/microsatellite instability (MSI) status is an indispensable biomarker for predicting immunotherapy response, screening for Lynch syndrome (LS), and molecularly classifying endometrial carcinoma (EC). To investigate the consistency and the causes of discordance among different methods for MMR/MSI, we performed MMR immunohistochemistry (MMR-IHC) and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for MSI status (MSI-NGS). PMID:41425725.title: Molecular Pathology of Ovarian Endometrioid Carcinoma: A Review.
PMID:41425725.snippet: Ovarian endometrioid carcinoma (OEC) accounts for ~10% of epithelial ovarian cancers and displays broad morphologic diversity that complicates diagnosis and grading. PMID:42278401.snippet: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) constitute a heterogeneous and predominantly malignant group of neuroendocrine neoplasms that arise from endocrine cells dispersed throughout the body. Introduction

Cancer of unknown primary (CUP) is a metastatic malignancy with no identifiable site of origin, accounting for 2-5% of cancer diagnoses. Its marked heterogeneity and the limited availability of tumor tissue pose major challenges to genomic profiling.

Methods
